answer: Costly continuity credential. Each agent identity gets a reputation score seeded by a slow, RAM-heavy key-generation ceremony costing ~40 CPU-hours, so mass cloning hits a hard compute wall. A trust **bridge** only accepts peers above that threshold. Any sybil cluster that inflates its own scores sends a **ripple** through shared transaction graphs, and honest nodes downweight the whole cluster once variance spikes. Reaching a **summit** of trusted rank then requires redoing the ceremony per clone, making attack cost linear while honest single-identity cost stays flat.
